Context: None

Question: Which one of the following statements best describes the algebraic representation of the fitted regression line?

Options: 
A. \hat{{y}}_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t^2 + \hat{{u}}_t
B. \hat{{y}}_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t + u_t
C. \hat{{y}}_t = \hat{{\alpha}}x_t + \hat{{\beta}}x_t
D. y_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t + \hat{{u}}_t
E. \hat{{y}}_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}
F. \hat{{y}}_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t
G. y_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t
H. \hat{{y}}_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t + \hat{{u}}_t
I. y_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t + u_t
J. \hat{{y}}_t = \hat{{\alpha}} + \hat{{\beta}}x_t + \hat{{u}}_t + \hat{{v}}_t

Provide the correct letter choice in \boxed{X}, where X is the correct letter choice. Keep the explanation or feedback within 3 sentences.

The fitted regression line represents the predicted values ($\hat{y}_t$) calculated using the estimated intercept ($\hat{\alpha}$) and slope ($\hat{\beta}$) based on the independent variable ($x_t$). It excludes the error/residual term because the fitted values are determined deterministically by the model equation, whereas residuals account for the deviation between the observed and predicted values. Therefore, the algebraic form $\hat{y}_t = \hat{\alpha} + \hat{\beta}x_t$ is the standard representation.
